question: On one communication-dependent HiddenBench verification task, does a phase-aware Exchange/Decide policy produce a different answer and cost profile than three-round natural discussion, and how does forced first-round disclosure behave?
scope: Single-task engineering/feasibility pilot only. This cannot establish protocol superiority, generalization, a scaling law, or an efficiency frontier.

model.name: Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M
model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202; RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8 GB; one slot; 24 GPU layers; 8192 context
model.cpu_resource_limit: --threads 4 --threads-batch 4; BelowNormal OS process priority where supported

conditions.name: natural_3
conditions.definition: Unmodified upstream natural discussion, limited to three rounds.

conditions.name: exchange_decide
conditions.definition: Rounds 1-2: each agent shares 1-2 decision-relevant facts and one reason the apparent front-runner could be wrong. Round 3: each agent summarizes strongest evidence and remaining uncertainty before separate final voting.

conditions.name: reveal_all_3
conditions.definition: Natural discussion for three rounds; mechanically append every fact available in the sender's local profile, verbatim, to each first-round message. Later messages are unmodified.

design.retry_policy: Upstream model client retries up to three times; invalid final votes may trigger up to three attempts. Count actual server completions separately from successful response slots.
design.persistence: Save one private raw result file after each condition. Do not publish raw task messages or visible facts.

predictions: Exchange/Decide may improve final accuracy over three-round natural discussion by eliciting and testing unique evidence; the single instance is descriptive only.
Reveal-All should maximize explicit first-round fact coverage by construction; lower accuracy despite complete disclosure would point to integration rather than surfacing in this episode.
The four-thread cap should lower peak host CPU use relative to the unbounded v0.5 service configuration, at possible cost to wall time. This is a resource prediction, not an assumed outcome.
outcomes: official HiddenBench initial and final individual/majority accuracy
semantic coverage of task-specific information in each transcript, annotated without exact-string-only matching
discussion transcript tokens and UTF-8 bytes
generated tokens, prompt-evaluation tokens, request count, service time, and truncations
host CPU and memory samples during inference
condition-level wall time and completion status
limits: One task, one profile, one seed, one model, and one run per condition.
The three-round natural baseline is matched in turns, not compared directly to v0.5's 15-round result.
Reveal-All changes disclosure policy and communication volume; it is a mechanistic diagnostic, not a bandwidth-matched codec comparison.

The runner reuses the pinned upstream task model, agent prompts, vote schema, and scorer but implements phase scheduling locally; it is not an exact reproduction of the paper's full 18-task, five-run study.
The four-thread setting has not yet been run. Stop if the user reports renewed system lag; do not exceed the frozen 60 nominal model-response calls.
